inputs.name: cassandra_version
inputs.description: Apache Cassandra 5.0 release to install, such as "5.0.9". Change cassandra_sha256 with it. Raising it installs the new release beside the old one and restarts Cassandra on it.

inputs.name: cassandra_sha256
inputs.description: SHA-256 of apache-cassandra-VERSION-bin.tar.gz, from the .sha256 file Apache publishes beside it. Change it with cassandra_version.

inputs.name: admin_password
inputs.description: Password for Cassandra's cassandra superuser, which the circuit changes from the default on the first apply. Pass it at run time with -var or TF_VAR_admin_password; it never reaches state or the plan.

inputs.name: cluster_name
inputs.description: cluster_name. Every node in a cluster needs the same one, and Cassandra refuses to start on data from a cluster with another name.

inputs.name: listen_address
inputs.description: IP address nodes talk to each other on, its listen_address. A host object's own listen_address wins over it, which a cluster needs since each node has its own.

inputs.name: rpc_address
inputs.description: IP address CQL clients connect to, its rpc_address. "0.0.0.0" listens on every address and tells clients the node's listen_address.

inputs.name: seeds
inputs.description: listen_address of the seed nodes new nodes contact to join, such as ["10.0.0.5", "10.0.0.6"]. When empty, each node is its own seed, which suits a single node.

inputs.name: heap_size
inputs.description: JVM heap, its MAX_HEAP_SIZE, such as "2G" or "512M". When null, Cassandra picks it from the host's memory: half of it up to 1G, or a quarter up to 8G, whichever is more.

inputs.name: settings
inputs.description: More cassandra.yaml settings, such as { concurrent_writes = 64, num_tokens = 8 }. Values can be maps and lists. The apply checks them before they replace the old file, and changing them restarts Cassandra.
